author: Aristotle
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Across his life and work, Aristotle saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?

originalQuote: The happy man lives well, and does well; for the things which are in his power to do he does, and he avoids the things which are not in his power to do.
